theorem_title: Euler valuation of finite relations among compact convex indicators
formal_statement:
namespace ConvexGeometry

theorem compact_convex_indicator_relation (n : ℕ)
    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (K : ι → Set (Fin n → ℝ)) (w : ι → ℚ)
    (hc : ∀ i, IsCompact (K i)) (hv : ∀ i, Convex ℝ (K i))
    (h : ∀ x, (∑ i, if x ∈ K i then w i else 0) = 0) :
    (∑ i, if (K i).Nonempty then w i else 0) = 0 := by
  sorry

end ConvexGeometry
natural_language_statement: Let finitely many compact convex subsets of a finite-dimensional real coordinate space carry rational weights. If the corresponding weighted sum of indicator functions vanishes at every point, then the sum of the weights of the nonempty sets is zero.
preamble:
import Mathlib

set_option autoImplicit false
attribute [local instance] Classical.propDecidable
source: The proof is an original Lean formalization using induction by coordinate slices. Its valuation and slicing strategy is inspired by Rolf Schneider, Combinatorial identities for polyhedral cones, Theorem 2.3 and equations (19)-(22), manuscript pages 6-8: https://home.mathematik.uni-freiburg.de/rschnei/Comb.Ident.rev.pdf. The submitted result is only the stated indicator-function relation; it is not a formalization of the paper's complete Euler or local-face theory.
